absence_arm_spec: When the register file EXISTS but holds zero data rows AND the verifier reports zero hits: PASS with an EMPTY note ('register empty, ratchet vacuous — nothing ruled because nothing fired'). NOT a failure: failing on empty would demand pre-registration, and pre-registration is laundering (ruling precedes row, per the register header). When the register is empty AND hits exist, the existing new-hits path already REDs (every hit unregistered) — no new arm needed for that case. The register-MISSING arm (REFUSE) is unchanged: a missing file cannot distinguish ruled from new, so refusal is the only honest output.
hole_confirmed: Stage 95 is WIRED (runs in the suite) while its four arms (baseline PASS, ruled-row-removed RED, register-missing REFUSE, dead-row PASS-with-STALE) are hand-run one-execution. A future edit inverting the ratchet (e.g., swapping the comm -23/-13 directions, which fails toward allowlist — the worst direction) would go green silently. Edit-time damage to shell control flow is observed, not theoretical (sync-docs.sh lost a record_repo call and gained a stale-abs clone bug in this same session, both caught only by reading output).
